title: Core common self Ext Tor complexes
statement: For schemes Z,Y [def-pc-scheme], a closed immersion i:Z -> Y [def-weil-closed-immersion], n in N, and the supplied derived category on Y [def-pc-derived-category], put B=i_*O_Z, S the degree-zero single functor, H=RHom_Y [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], G=H^n(H(B[0],B[0])), and Q=i*H^(-n)(B[0] tensor^L B[0]) [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. There exist an additivity witness for i*, cochain complexes P on Y and J on Z [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], augmentations a:P -> B[0] and b:O_Z[0] -> J which are quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], P K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and J K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For the actual termwise tensor pullback T=i*P, there are vanishing statements H^k(J)=0 for k != 0, and isomorphisms H^0(J) with O_Z, i*G with H^n(Hom(T,J)) [def-pur-hom-complex], and Q with H^(-n)(T). No local finite-free condition is asserted here.

source.place: duality.tex, lemma-regular-ideal-ext, together with tags 08DH, 08I3, 08KS and 068G for the derived pullback, internal Hom and tensor identifications.

proof.text: Obtain a K-flat resolution P of B[0] with flat terms from exists_isKFlatResolution. Obtain the functorial K-injective resolution of O_Z[0] from grothendieckAbelian_and_functorial_kInjective_resolutions. Tensor pullback is additive by its adjunction with the additive pushforward. Define T as its termwise application to P. Homology of the quasi-isomorphism b and Mathlib homology of a single complex give the vanishing hJ and the degree-zero isomorphism e0.

Apply the two fixed-resolution comparisons in arbitrary integer degrees to obtain G isomorphic to i_*H^n(Hom(T,J)) and H^(-n)(B[0] tensor^L B[0]) isomorphic to i_*H^(-n)(T). Apply ordinary tensor pullback to these isomorphisms, then compose with the invertible closed-immersion counit. This constructs eG and eQ for the same P and J chosen in step 1. Return the resolutions, their augmentations, flat terms, quasi-isomorphisms, K-injectivity, homology vanishing and these three isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_selfExt_tor_resolution_core
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (n : ℕ) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let G := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (n : ℤ)).obj
        (H.obj (op (S.obj B), S.obj B))
    let Q := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (-(n : ℤ))).obj
          (S.obj B ⊗ S.obj B))
    ∃ (_add : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).Additive)
      (P : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ) (J : CochainComplex Z.Modules ℤ)
      (a : P ⟶ (HomologicalComplex.single Y.Modules (.up ℤ) 0).obj B)
      (b : (HomologicalComplex.single Z.Modules (.up ℤ) 0).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf) ⟶ J),
      CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolution (R := Y.sheaf) a ∧
      (∀ k : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (P.X k)) ∧
      QuasiIso b ∧ J.IsKInjective ∧
      let T := ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P
      ∃ (hJ : ∀ k : ℤ, k ≠ 0 → IsZero (J.homology k))
      (e0 : J.homology 0 ≅ SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
      (eG : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj G ≅
        (homComplex (R := Z.sheaf) T J).homology (n : ℤ))
      (eQ : Q ≅ T.homology (-(n : ℤ))), True
